subject: Urgent: EcomPulse latency & token velocity choke — experiencing p95/p99 regressions
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice@ecompulse.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@ecompulse.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:12:15 -0800
Subject: Host API token velocity / p95/p99 regressions (started after maintenance)

Connor —

We started seeing a sharp regression across our hosted API requests this morning after what looked like a Redwood platform maintenance window overnight. Quick summary:
- p95 latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms across our main route
- p99 is now spiking to 800–1,200ms (previously ~280–320ms)
- Token-per-second throughput (observed from client-side metrics) dropped from ~460 tps -> ~110 tps for the same batched payloads

This is impacting revenue-critical flows (cart scoring) and hurting user-facing SLAs. We noticed the problem coincided with model selector/quant changes deployed around 03:30 UTC per our traffic window.

Attached is a dashboard snapshot and an exported CSV of a 2-hour window. Can you escalate and advise next steps or a rollback option? We need mitigation within the next 2–3 hours if possible.

Thanks,
Alice Moreno
Head of Product, EcomPulse
alice@ecompulse.com
(Attachment: ecompulse_p95_p99_dashboard_20270111.png)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:06:41 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Host API token velocity / p95/p99 regressions (started after maintenance)

Forwarding Alice's note — high priority customer escalation (EcomPulse, DEAL-7894).

Quick context: Customer reports token/sec collapse and p95/p99 spike that aligns with our overnight rollout. They are seeing production impact on cart scoring.

Asks:
- Engineering (Marissa/Markus): Triage and confirm if kernel selector / quant profile change rolled at ~03:30 UTC caused this. If confirmed, propose immediate mitigations (rollback, pin to previous model variant, or localized config change).
- CS (Laura): Acknowledge to the customer, share proposed mitigation, and request traffic samples/logs if needed.

Attaching the customer's snapshot and our internal kernel selector diff that landed in the window (kernel_selector_change.diff).

Connor O'Brien
Account Exec — North America
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: kernel_selector_change.diff)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:30:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Host API token velocity / p95/p99 regressions (started after maintenance)

Thanks for flagging — triage notes below.

What we know so far:
- We rolled a kernel-selector/quant profile update at 03:27 UTC (change set: kernel_selector_change.diff). The change prioritized a new quantized kernel path for Llama-variant instances to reduce GPU memory, with an aggressive fallback threshold.
- Canary signals looked fine for standard latency distributions, but our canary traffic didn't include the customer-specific long-context batched patterns used by EcomPulse (their request shape: batch=8, seq_len~2048 with prefix caching).
- Infra traces show increased token generation time on nodes running the new kernel path: token generation latency per step doubled on average for the affected sequences.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Rollback the kernel-selector change for host pool serving EcomPulse (fastest; ~15–20m to push and warm).
2) Force-route EcomPulse traffic to the previous model variant (pin model_version=v2026-12-10) until we complete a deeper perf regression analysis.
3) Tune quant fallback thresholds to prefer the older kernel for high seq_len requests, but this requires a staged deploy and extra validation.

I recommend option #1 followed by targeted perf tests using their sample traces. Markus / infra: can you confirm whether we have a one-button rollback for the selector change and if it can be constrained by host pool tag? If yes, I will coordinate the rollback and perf verification.

Marissa Cole
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: perf_trace_snippets.log)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@ecompulse.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:45:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Host API token velocity / p95/p99 regressions (started after maintenance)

Hi Alice —

Thank you for the quick heads-up and the dashboard snapshot. We're treating this as a priority incident. Immediate plan:
- We're validating whether the kernel-selector/quant rollout from last night correlates (internal triage underway).
- Short-term mitigation we can offer right now: pin your traffic to the previous model variant (v2026-12-10) or route your traffic to a dedicated pool that hasn't received the selector change. This will preserve behavior while we investigate.

Could you share a 2–3 minute trace/sample of a failing request (including request headers and timings)? That will speed up reproduction on our side. If you prefer, we can apply the pin on your behalf and monitor the effect.

We're aiming to have a mitigation in place within 90 minutes. I'll update you as soon as we have confirmation from infra.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Host API token velocity / p95/p99 regressions (started after maintenance)

Looping in Aditya for exec visibility.

Agree with Marissa — prioritize rollback for the affected host pool. Actions I am authorizing now:
- Infra: initiate rollback of kernel-selector change for pools tagged "prod-ecompulse" (if tags not present, rollback globally and narrow thereafter).
- Eng: run targeted perf tests with EcomPulse traces during rollback warm-up window.
- CS: apply customer pin (Laura) if rollback cannot be completed within 25 minutes.

We need a short, clear customer-facing timeline: ETA for mitigation and when we'll confirm metrics are back to baseline. Connor/Laura: please share that with the customer. I want a postmortem scheduled within 48 hours to cover gaps in canary coverage and test matrix.

Markus Klein
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 13:22:44 -08:00
Subject: Re: Host API token velocity / p95/p99 regressions (started after maintenance) — rollback complete

Update and resolution: rollback completed at 12:58 PST for the affected host pool (rolled kernel-selector to previous baseline). Post-rollback observations:
- p95 returned to ~130ms within the first 10 minutes after warm-up; p99 back to ~320ms.
- Token-per-second throughput for EcomPulse test trace returned to ~440 tps (previously observed 110 tps).
- We captured traces and will run a regression suite to surface the exact code path divergence (logs attached: perf_snapshot_before_after.csv).

Next steps:
- Schedule a short postmortem (Marissa + Markus + Infra + CS) within 48 hours to review canary blind spots and update our rollout checklist to include long-seq/batched patterns.
- Create a hotfix plan that preserves memory benefits of the new path without regressing high-sequence batched workloads (quant fallback tuning + improved selector heuristics).

Thanks everyone for the rapid response. Connor/Laura: please confirm with EcomPulse and close the loop.

Marissa Cole
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: perf_snapshot_before_after.csv)
